key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: GRADUAL onset over days to weeks (chronic obstruction), may have acute exacerbation. History of peptic ulcer disease or gastric malignancy. LOCATION: Epigastric (upper mid-abdomen), may radiate to back. DURATION: CONSTANT discomfort with episodic severe pain during eating. CHARACTER: CRAMPY, fullness, bloating initially. Becomes CONSTANT dull ache if severe. AGGRAVATING: Eating solid foods markedly worsens symptoms. Nausea and vomiting occur 30min-2hrs after eating. RELIEVING: Vomiting provides temporary relief of distension. Liquids tolerated better than solids initially. TIMING: Postprandial (after meals), progressive worsening over time. SEVERITY: 5-7/10, moderate. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: Persistent or projectile vomiting of UNDIGESTED FOOD (hours old), early satiety, weight loss, visible gastric peristalsis (succussion splash), dehydration. Vomit may contain food from >12 hours ago. KEY POSITIVES: Vomiting undigested food, early satiety, weight loss, history of PUD or gastric cancer. KEY NEGATIVES: Bilious vomiting suggests obstruction beyond duodenum (different diagnosis).

red_flags: Severe dehydration with hypotension - needs IV fluids immediately
Coffee-ground emesis or hematemesis - bleeding ulcer
Severe electrolyte imbalances - hypochloremic, hypokalemic alkalosis
